questions.question: What is XSS and how do you prevent it in Rails?
questions.title: XSS Basics
questions.direct_answer: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) is injecting malicious HTML/JS into a page. If you render user input un-escaped, an attacker can run scripts in other users' browsers: a comment with `<script>steal(document.cookie)</script>` runs when others view it. Rails prevents it by DEFAULT: ERB's `<%= ... %>` HTML-escapes everything (turns <, >, & into <, >) so the script shows as text, not code. You opt OUT of escaping with `<%= raw ... %>` or `<%== ... %>` (the 'raw' form) — only do this on TRUSTED content, or sanitize it first with `sanitize` (a whitelist). In API-only apps (JSON), the risk is lower but still escape on the client. Don't build HTML by string concatenation with user input; use the auto-escaping templates. The rule: escape by default (Rails does), and only un-escape/sanitize when you've validated the content.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Rails escapes ERB output by default (<%= %>), preventing XSS, and raw/sanitize opt out carefully.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using `raw` or `<%==` on untrusted content (XSS — escape by default; sanitize first).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: XSS = injecting HTML/JS into a page. Rails escapes <%= %> by default. Opt out with raw/<%== only on trusted/sanitized content.

sections.title: Escape by Default
sections.content: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) is injecting malicious HTML or JS into a page. If you render user input un-escaped, an attacker can run scripts in other users' browsers: a comment with script steal document cookie script runs when others view it. Rails prevents it by DEFAULT: ERB's percent equals percent HTML-escapes everything (turns less-than, greater-than, ampersand into entities) so the script shows as text, not code. You opt OUT of escaping with raw or the double-equals form — only do this on TRUSTED content, or sanitize it first with sanitize (a whitelist). In API-only apps (JSON), the risk is lower but still escape on the client. Don't build HTML by string concatenation with user input; use the auto-escaping templates. The rule: escape by default (Rails does), and only un-escape or sanitize when you've validated the content.

sections.title: XSS
sections.content:
inject HTML/JS. Rails escapes <%= %> by default. raw/<%== opts out (trusted only). sanitize = whitelist.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[user input: <script>] --> E[<%= %>: escaped]
  E --> S[shows as text]
  R[raw / <%==] --> N[NOT escaped -> runs]
  N --> X[XSS if untrusted]
```

sections.title: XSS
sections.content:
```ruby # ERB: <%=%> ESCAPES by default (Rails) -> prevents XSS <%# comment %> <%= @comment.body %> # ' # <%= raw @comment.body %> -> the script RUNS in other users' browsers # DON'T build HTML by string concatenation with user input: # "
#{user_input}
".html_safe # XSS (html_safe opts out of escaping) # Use templates with auto-escaping; mark html_safe only on TRUSTED strings. # In JSON APIs, the risk is lower, but still escape on the CLIENT when rendering. # Rule: escape by default (Rails does); un-escape/sanitize only on validated content. # Avoid: raw, html_safe, <%== on any user-controlled value. ```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using `raw` or `<%==` or `.html_safe` on untrusted content (XSS — escape by default).
Building HTML by string concatenation with user input (use auto-escaping templates).
Forgetting sanitize uses a whitelist (still strip script tags).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: XSS = injecting malicious HTML/JS into a page that runs in other users' browsers.
Rails escapes ERB output by default (<%= %> turns <, >, & into entities).
Opt out with raw / <%== / .html_safe — only on TRUSTED or sanitized content.
sanitize whitelists safe tags (b, i, a) and strips script.
Don't build HTML by string concatenation with user input; escape by default.
